_readme: Suppressions for the ChainGPT contract audit gate (scripts/chaingpt-audit.mjs).
The gate fails the build when the auditor reports a finding at or above severityFloor. An
entry below removes exactly one finding, named by the deterministic findingId that
packages/chaingpt/src/auditor.ts derives as '<path>:<SEVERITY>:<slugified-title>'.
WHEN SUPPRESSING IS LEGITIMATE. Two cases, and no others.
1. The finding is factually wrong about this code. A model that flags 'block.timestamp
manipulation' against a contract whose only time windows are a 2-day governance timelock
and a multi-hour oracle staleness bound is comparing a 12-second validator drift to a
day-scale threshold. Both statements are true and they are not about the same thing.
2. The finding describes a real vulnerability class that is structurally impossible here,
and the reason names the mechanism that makes it impossible - a role guard, a checked
bound, a frozen enum ordinal - with the file and line that enforces it. 'Reviewed, not
exploitable' is not a reason. It is a summary of a reason that was never written down.
It is never legitimate to suppress because a fix is inconvenient, because the finding is hard
to understand, or because a release needs to be green. Those are open issues. An issue that
blocks a merge is doing its job; a suppression that hides one is a decision to ship the risk,
and the only honest way to make that decision is in a reviewed diff to this file.
WHAT THE GATE ENFORCES ON THIS FILE. A malformed entry fails the run rather than being
skipped, because a suppression that silently does not apply and a suppression that silently
does are the same kind of surprise.
- severityFloor is one of INFO, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL
- reason is at least 40 characters and says why the finding does not apply to this code
- reviewer names the person who checked it, not a team and not a tool
- addedOn is YYYY-MM-DD; expiresOn is YYYY-MM-DD or null
- an expired entry stops suppressing, is reported loudly, and the finding blocks again
- findingId matching is exact. There are deliberately no wildcards, because a pattern
suppresses findings nobody has read yet
The list is empty. Every finding from every run is recorded in full under
artifacts/security/chaingpt/<commit>.json, which is gitignored, so this file is the only
durable record of a judgement call and has to carry the argument rather than point at one.
Entry shape:
"findingId": "contracts/src/core/ClearingHouse.sol:MEDIUM:some-title",
"reason": "why this does not apply here, naming the mechanism and where it is enforced",
"reviewer": "Name Surname",
"expiresOn": null
